Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going to (4,1,2), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going to (6,1,4), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So my guess (to (4,1,4) from cell (2,1,4)) was wrong, so the line must go to (2,1,2).

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going to (4,1,4), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going to (6,1,2), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So my guess (to (2,6,7) from cell (2,7,6)) was wrong, so the line must go to (1,6,6).

Contradiction! Going to (1,2,4) would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order), and that's the only legal move. So my guess (to (1,4,4) from cell (1,4,6)) was wrong, so the line must go to (1,2,6).
I can't rule out to (2,1,6) or to (2,2,7) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (2,1,6).

The line must go to (6,1,6): to (7,2,6) is number 21, which comes later.
Going to (6,1,4) would strand number 10: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes to (4,1,6).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (4,1,4).
